text: Deep learning classification of land cover from multispectral satellite imagery. Accurate land cover mapping supports environmental monitoring. This study compares convolutional and transformer architectures for classification of multispectral satellite scenes across heterogeneous landscapes, using harmonised training samples and consistent evaluation protocols. Transfer learning from pretrained backbones is assessed. Results indicate modest gains from transformer architectures at higher computational cost, and class confusion persists between built-up and bare soil categories.
label: Not related

text: Virtual reality assessment of crossing decisions among older adults. Understanding decision making at crossings supports safety intervention design. Participants completed simulated road crossing tasks in an immersive virtual environment under varying traffic gap distributions and visual complexity. Decision latency, accepted gap size and collision incidence were recorded by the simulation. Older participants accepted smaller gaps under high visual complexity, and results are discussed in relation to training interventions; no measurement of real street environments was undertaken.
label: Not related

text: Estimating origin-destination flows from public transport smartcard records. Understanding travel patterns supports service planning. Smartcard transaction records were processed with destination inference algorithms and validated against a sample of surveyed journeys. Temporal profiles and transfer patterns were derived at stop level. The resulting matrices support timetable adjustment and were compared against previous survey-based estimates, showing systematic differences in off-peak periods.
label: Not related

text: Inertial gait analysis for early detection of mobility decline in community-dwelling older adults. Subtle changes in walking may precede functional decline. Participants wore lumbar-mounted inertial sensors during standardised and free-living walking bouts over one week. Gait speed, cadence, step regularity and variability were extracted and compared against clinical assessment scores. Several derived parameters distinguished participants with declining function, supporting sensor-based screening in community settings.
label: Not related

text: Public participation geographic information systems for identifying valued walking routes. Resident knowledge can complement technical assessment. An online mapping platform invited residents to identify routes they valued and to annotate perceived problems. Contributions were analysed spatially and thematically, and compared against municipal priority networks. Substantial divergence was found, with residents emphasising informal paths absent from official networks; no instrumentation or automated measurement was involved.
label: Not related

text: Modelling urban heat island intensity from meteorological station networks and land cover. Understanding heat island dynamics informs adaptation planning. This study combines records from a regional meteorological station network with satellite-derived land cover fractions to model canopy layer heat island intensity across a metropolitan region. Regression and machine learning specifications are compared. Impervious fraction and distance to water bodies were the dominant predictors, and model outputs were used to delineate priority adaptation zones.
label: Not related

text: Reinforcement learning for socially aware robot motion among pedestrians. Service robots operating in pedestrian spaces must move predictably. This work trains a policy that anticipates pedestrian intent from short observation windows and generates motion respecting social distance conventions. Training used a mixture of simulated crowds and recorded trajectory datasets. Evaluation in a pedestrianised area demonstrated reduced intrusion into personal space compared with a baseline planner while maintaining goal completion rates.
label: Not related

text: Association between transit accessibility and car ownership in metropolitan households. Reducing car dependence is a policy objective in many regions. This study computes transit accessibility from scheduled service data and network analysis, and relates it to car ownership reported in a household travel survey. Ordered response models control for income, household composition and residential self-selection. Accessibility was inversely associated with ownership, though the effect size was modest after accounting for residential preferences.
label: Not related

text: Evaluating a school-based active travel promotion programme. Encouraging walking and cycling to school has health and environmental benefits. This evaluation compared intervention and control schools using repeated hands-up surveys of travel mode and parent questionnaires over two academic years. Difference-in-difference models estimated programme effect. Modest increases in walking were observed at intervention schools, concentrated among children living within one kilometre; environmental conditions were not measured.
label: Not related

text: An automated framework for sidewalk width, longitudinal grade and cross-slope. Standard mapping products gave no reliable indication of sidewalk width, longitudinal grade and cross-slope along the walking network of a desert city exposed to extreme heat. The field campaign covered 252 footway sections in a desert city exposed to extreme heat. Using a backpack-mounted lidar scanner integrated with inertial navigation, the team isolated the pedestrian surface and reconstructed a continuous three-dimensional profile. To assess measurement error, 97 sites were revisited with a second acquisition platform operating on the same route. Results showed that older street segments contained clusters of slopes and width restrictions that were absent from the municipal inventory. Temporal replication showed that the detected pattern was not explained solely by weather or day of week. These measurements provide a reproducible basis to support accessibility audits and prioritise barrier-removal works.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Street-image detection of curb-ramp condition in a polycentric European city. Municipal datasets for a polycentric European city recorded nominal infrastructure but omitted the local variation in curb-ramp provision and condition at pedestrian crossings. To retain street-level variation, georeferenced street-level imagery processed with an object-detection network collected data at 195 crossing approaches; the subsequent analysis located ramp faces, tactile warnings and missing transitions at each corner. Outputs attached to the pedestrian network included ramp presence, surface condition, alignment and detectable-warning coverage. Temporal replication showed that the detected pattern was not explained solely by weather or day of week. A stratified validation exercise compared the estimates with duplicate traversals completed on different days at 97 sites. Across the study area, the strongest result was that missing or misaligned ramps were concentrated around arterial intersections and older housing estates. This pedestrian-scale evidence can be used to update crossing inventories and identify routes that remain inaccessible.

The authors applied smartphone and wheelchair-mounted inertial sensors to 235 route sections and converted vertical acceleration into a segment-level roughness indicator after speed correction. Data quality checks removed periods affected by sensor drift, occlusion or poor satellite reception. The workflow was designed to help practitioners improve independent navigation for visitors and cognitively vulnerable users.

text: Methods for neighbourhood walkability and physical activity. The wearable device measured the participants' activity, not a dimension of the walking environment. A separate pedestrian-scale campaign would be needed to characterise the walking environment. A network of calibrated acoustic nodes was installed along pedestrian streets and recorded equivalent and percentile sound levels continuously for eight months. Spectral descriptors were computed and clustered to distinguish traffic-dominated from activity-dominated soundscapes. Segments classified as activity-dominated coincided with locations exhibiting higher observed pedestrian dwell time.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Low-cost sensor network for monitoring pedestrian-level air quality along school routes. Children walking to school may experience elevated pollutant exposure. Calibrated low-cost nitrogen dioxide and particulate sensors were installed at pedestrian height along designated school routes and co-located with a reference monitor for calibration. Hourly concentrations were mapped and compared between route alternatives. Interior street alternatives showed consistently lower concentrations, and the measured differentials informed revision of recommended school route designations.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Thermal comfort mapping of pedestrian networks using bicycle-mounted mobile sensing. Systematic characterisation of microclimate along pedestrian routes requires dense spatial sampling. A bicycle-mounted instrument package recorded air temperature, humidity, wind speed and mean radiant temperature along repeated transects covering the pedestrian network of a mid-sized city. Data were corrected for sensor response time and aggregated by street segment. Derived comfort indices identified a consistent set of thermally disadvantaged corridors linking residential areas to transit.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Fixed camera observation of pedestrian crossing behaviour and infrastructure adequacy. Crossing provision can be evaluated by observing how it is actually used. Fixed cameras recorded pedestrian crossing movements at twelve intersections, and an automated tracking pipeline extracted crossing trajectories, waiting times and non-compliant crossings. Observed behaviour was related to measured crossing geometry and signal timing. Intersections with longer crossing distances and shorter clearance intervals exhibited higher rates of incomplete crossings.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Georeferenced video and machine learning for auditing sidewalk accessibility barriers. Manual accessibility audits are difficult to scale. A pedestrian-borne camera with GNSS logging captured continuous video along the footway network, and a detection model identified barriers including steps, poles, temporary signage and surface breaks. Detections were georeferenced and aggregated to segments. Agreement with expert manual audit reached substantial levels, and the resulting barrier map supported prioritisation of remediation works.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Sky view factor derived from fisheye imagery for pedestrian solar exposure assessment. Solar access at pedestrian level governs both summer discomfort and winter usability. Fisheye images were captured at pedestrian height at a systematic sample of points and processed to compute sky view factor and directional solar obstruction. Values were validated against measurements derived from surveyed building geometry. The resulting maps identified street orientations where summer exposure and winter shading simultaneously reach unfavourable values.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Wearable multi-sensor assessment of walking environments at a transport interchange. Automated characterisation of walking conditions can reduce reliance on surveys. A wearable system combining inertial sensors, barometric altimetry and a forward-facing camera was used to classify walking environments encountered at a transport interchange, distinguishing level surfaces, ramps, stairs and uneven paving. Several classifiers were compared and the best configuration exceeded 90 percent accuracy against annotated ground truth, enabling automated profiling of access routes.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Detecting vegetation encroachment on footways from mobile imagery and range data. Overgrown vegetation reduces effective walking width and forces pedestrians onto the carriageway. Mobile mapping imagery and lidar returns were processed to detect vegetation intruding into the pedestrian clearance envelope, quantifying intrusion depth and height. Detections were compared with maintenance complaint records. Automated detection identified substantially more encroachment locations than the complaint-driven process, most of them on low-traffic residential streets.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Illuminance and luminance mapping of pedestrian underpasses using calibrated imaging. Underpasses concentrate perceived insecurity within pedestrian networks. Calibrated luminance imaging and point illuminance measurement were carried out in fourteen underpasses at night, producing spatial distributions of light level, uniformity and glare. Measured metrics were compared against design guidance and against user ratings collected on site. Uniformity, rather than mean illuminance, showed the strongest association with reported reassurance.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Pedestrian volume estimation from wireless signal detection on commercial streets. Continuous pedestrian counts support evaluation of streetscape investment. Wireless probe request detection was deployed on commercial streets, with detection rates calibrated against synchronised manual counts and correction factors estimated for device carriage rates. Continuous volume estimates were produced for eighteen months spanning a public realm improvement. Post-intervention volumes rose significantly relative to comparison streets after controlling for weather and seasonality.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Land use mix and transport mode share in medium-sized European cities. Diversity of land use is a recognised correlate of travel behaviour. This study computes entropy-based land use mix indicators from cadastral records for medium-sized cities and relates them to mode share reported in national travel surveys. Multilevel models control for household characteristics and city size. Land use mix showed a positive association with walking mode share, though the magnitude varied considerably between national contexts.
label: Not related

text: Machine learning prediction of street tree failure risk. Tree failure poses risks to property and people in cities. This study applied regression trees and ensemble methods to predict failure using attributes obtainable in routine field inspection, including species, diameter, surrounding building height and district age. Models were trained on municipal failure records over a decade. Surrounding building height and district age emerged as the dominant predictors, supporting risk-based scheduling of preventive maintenance.
label: Not related

text: Evaluating a virtual reality protocol for streetscape preference elicitation. Immersive environments offer controlled presentation of design alternatives. Participants viewed reconstructed street scenes in a head-mounted display and rated preference and perceived quality across systematically varied design parameters. Ratings were analysed with mixed models. The protocol produced consistent preference orderings, and its reliability relative to photographic presentation is discussed; no measurement of existing physical environments was undertaken.
label: Not related

text: Automated litter detection from vehicle imagery for street cleansing operations. Efficient allocation of cleansing resources requires knowledge of where waste accumulates. Imagery collected from municipal service vehicles was processed with a detection model to identify litter, fly-tipping and overflowing bins along carriageways. Detections were aggregated by route and compared with existing complaint-driven scheduling. The system enabled reallocation of cleansing rounds and reduced repeat complaints in the pilot district.
label: Not related

text: Association between green space proximity and mental health outcomes. Access to green space has been linked to psychological wellbeing. This cohort analysis linked residential addresses to green space proximity computed from land cover databases and examined associations with validated mental health instruments over follow-up. Models adjusted for individual and area-level confounders. Proximity to green space was associated with modestly better outcomes, with associations stronger among lower-income participants.
label: Not related

text: Detecting handrails, steps and level changes along pedestrian routes with mobile range sensing. Vertical discontinuities determine route feasibility for many pedestrians. Mobile range sensing captured pedestrian routes, and a processing chain identified steps, ramps, level changes and the presence of handrails, recording their dimensions. Field verification confirmed detection reliability. A substantial share of level changes exceeding the accessible threshold lacked any handrail, and their spatial distribution was concentrated on connections between residential terraces and the main street network.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Automated assessment of crossing sight lines using street-level imagery and geometry reconstruction. Visibility between pedestrians and drivers at crossings is a determinant of safety. Street-level imagery and reconstructed geometry were used to compute available sight distance from typical pedestrian waiting positions at crossings, accounting for parked vehicles, vegetation and street furniture detected in the same imagery. Computed sight distances were validated against on-site measurement. Obstruction by permitted parking reduced sight distance below recommended values at a large fraction of unsignalised crossings.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Sensing footway surface temperature and moisture to characterise slip and heat conditions. Surface state affects both slip risk and thermal comfort. A pedestrian-borne rig combining infrared surface thermometry and a moisture sensor traversed footways across seasons, and readings were georeferenced and aggregated by segment and material. Shaded stone surfaces retained moisture substantially longer after rainfall, and exposed asphalt reached surface temperatures that coincided with locations of reported discomfort in a parallel survey.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Measuring visual attention to hazards during walking with mobile eye tracking. Whether pedestrians notice hazards depends on the visual environment. Participants walked routes containing typical hazards such as raised slabs, bollards and cyclist crossings while wearing mobile eye-tracking glasses, with gaze mapped onto segmented imagery of the same locations. Fixation on hazards was related to visual clutter measured from the imagery. Detection of low-contrast hazards declined markedly in visually complex settings, with implications for hazard marking.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Continuous footway counts using stereo cameras to evaluate a pedestrianisation scheme. Robust evaluation requires continuous measurement over an adequate period. Stereo cameras with automated detection recorded footway volumes and directional flows at treated and comparison streets for six months before and twelve months after a pedestrianisation scheme. Counts were validated against manual observation. Volumes on treated streets increased and stationary activity rose disproportionately, while comparison streets showed no equivalent change.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Assessing pedestrian exposure to traffic noise and vibration on narrow footways. Narrow footways place pedestrians close to moving traffic. Sound level meters and triaxial vibration sensors were mounted at pedestrian height on footways of differing width along comparable traffic corridors, recording continuously for one month. Exposure metrics were computed and related to measured lateral separation from the carriageway. Both noise and perceptible vibration declined steeply with lateral separation, with the sharpest gradient in the first metre.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Detection of pedestrian route obstruction by vegetation using seasonal imagery comparison. Vegetation growth intermittently obstructs footways. Street imagery captured in successive seasons was registered and compared to detect vegetation intruding into the pedestrian clearance envelope, quantifying intrusion depth and persistence. Detections were verified in the field. Persistent intrusions concentrated on segments adjacent to private gardens, where maintenance responsibility is ambiguous, and were largely absent from the municipal complaint record.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Mapping pedestrian-level air flow and pollutant dispersion with distributed sensing in a street canyon. Ventilation of street canyons governs pollutant accumulation at pedestrian height. A distributed array of anemometers and particulate sensors was installed at pedestrian height along a canyon of uniform geometry, recording for one year. Measured flow regimes were classified by ambient wind direction and related to observed concentration. Concentrations under perpendicular wind conditions exceeded parallel conditions by a wide margin on the leeward footway.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Longitudinal cohort analysis of neighbourhood change and self-reported walking. Residential context evolves over time. This analysis linked repeated survey waves to time-varying neighbourhood characteristics derived from administrative sources, examining whether changes in the residential context were associated with changes in reported walking. Fixed effects models controlled for time-invariant individual characteristics. Modest associations were observed for changes in destination availability, and no environmental measurement was undertaken by the authors.
label: Not related

text: Optimising bus stop placement using scheduled service and demand data. Stop spacing balances access and speed. This study formulates stop placement as an optimisation problem using demand estimated from smartcard records and walking access computed on the street network. Alternative spacing scenarios are evaluated against access and running time objectives. Results indicate scope for consolidation on suburban corridors without material access penalty for most passengers.
label: Not related

text: Modelling flood risk to pedestrian networks using terrain and drainage data. Flooding disrupts pedestrian movement. Terrain models and drainage network records were used to simulate surface water accumulation under design rainfall scenarios, and results were intersected with the pedestrian network to identify segments likely to become impassable. No field measurement of flood conditions was conducted, and validation relied on historical incident reports.
label: Not related

text: Comparative evaluation of activity monitor placement in free-living conditions. Device placement affects measurement validity. Participants simultaneously wore monitors at wrist, hip and thigh during free-living conditions for one week, and outputs were compared for activity classification and intensity estimation. Agreement varied by activity type, with the largest discrepancies for cycling and stair climbing. Recommendations for placement selection in population studies are provided.
label: Not related

text: Simulating pedestrian flows in a redesigned transport interchange. Design alternatives can be compared before construction. A microscopic pedestrian model was calibrated using published behavioural parameters and applied to alternative interchange layouts under forecast demand. Level of service, queue formation and transfer times were compared across alternatives. The preferred layout reduced modelled transfer times; field validation is proposed for the operational phase.
label: Not related

text: Estimating tree canopy cover from airborne lidar for municipal reporting. Canopy targets require consistent measurement. Airborne lidar acquired for a metropolitan area was processed to delineate canopy and compute cover fractions by administrative unit, with accuracy assessed against field plots. Trends across two acquisition epochs were reported. The workflow supports statutory canopy reporting and relies exclusively on airborne acquisition.
label: Not related

text: Smartphone recognition of commuting modes in a working-age cohort. Participants carried phones that recorded accelerometry, gyroscope and location signals during routine travel. A supervised model classified walking, cycling, public transport and private-car stages, with travel diaries providing reference labels. Accuracy was highest for motorised modes and lower for short transfers. The resulting mode histories were used to study commuting behaviour rather than to characterise sidewalks, crossings or other pedestrian-environment conditions.
label: Not related

text: Measuring doorway density and frontage setbacks with monocular street imagery. Frequent entrances and shallow setbacks can support active and engaging walking environments. In the reported study, a computer-vision pipeline estimated ground-floor planes, detected public entrances and measured their setback from the footway across mixed-use streets. Entrance density varied substantially within commercial districts and was positively associated with observed pedestrian stopping activity. Derived indicators were compared with architectural drawings and a manual frontage audit.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Heart-rate response to a neighbourhood walking programme. Adults with low baseline activity joined supervised group walks for twelve weeks while chest straps recorded heart rate and consumer trackers counted steps. Changes in fitness, adherence and perceived exertion were compared with a wait-list group. Participants improved walking endurance, but gains differed by attendance. Environmental conditions along the routes were held constant and were not measured as study outcomes.
label: Not related

text: Green-space proximity, physical activity and cardiometabolic risk. Vegetation and park access were calculated from satellite products and administrative boundaries, while participants wore accelerometers and underwent clinical assessment. Path models tested whether physical activity mediated associations with health. This cohort linked residential environmental exposure to health indicators. Greater park proximity was associated with more activity, but mediation of cardiometabolic outcomes was modest.
label: Not related

text: Detecting temporary narrowing of sidewalks with repeated mobile mapping. Construction barriers and delivery activity produce time-dependent restrictions that static maps cannot represent. Methodologically, a vehicle-mounted imaging and range system traversed the same commercial corridors at four times of day over twelve weeks, estimating effective width after detecting cones, hoardings, parked vehicles and stored goods. Spot checks by observers confirmed the temporal classifications. Narrowing was most persistent during morning deliveries and affected routes serving two major bus interchanges.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Wheelchair vibration sensing for evaluating transitions between paving materials. Surface transitions can create discomfort even when each paving material is individually compliant. Manual wheelchairs equipped with tri-axial accelerometers crossed joints between asphalt, concrete, stone and tactile paving at controlled speeds. Signal features were calibrated against profilometer measurements and repeated by users of different body mass. The largest vibration peaks occurred at poorly aligned material boundaries rather than on the roughest continuous surfaces.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Built environment and body mass trajectories in a national child cohort. Longitudinal models assessed how residential context related to changes in body mass. Environmental exposures were linked from land-use parcels, road networks and service databases, while height and weight were repeatedly measured. Associations were estimated over six survey waves. Access to destinations was associated with slower increases in body mass, whereas road density showed no stable relationship.
label: Not related

text: Thermal imaging and moisture sensing of winter slip hazards on footpaths. A pedestrian-borne rig combined downward thermal imagery, surface moisture probes and GNSS while traversing priority walking routes before sunrise. Freeze-thaw cycles create localised hazards that are not captured by general weather observations. Observed ice patches were verified with friction measurements at selected locations. Persistent low-friction sections clustered near shaded drainage outlets and remained hazardous after adjacent carriageways had cleared.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Transit-oriented development and self-reported transport walking. Station access and land-use intensity were derived from scheduled service and parcel databases, and walking was reported in household surveys. Researchers investigated whether living near high-frequency transit encouraged walking for transport. Multilevel models compared residents across station areas. Residents near frequent transit reported more transport walking, particularly among households without a private vehicle.
label: Not related

text: Crowdsourced smartphone sensing of footway roughness after utility works. Reinstated trenches may degrade walking comfort across otherwise well-maintained pavements. To address this, participants carried smartphones in standardised waist pouches while walking routes affected by recent utility works, and vertical acceleration was converted to a segment-level roughness measure. Engineer ratings and laser profiles provided reference observations. Newly reinstated sections showed highly variable performance, allowing the authority to target contractors for remedial inspection.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Image-based monitoring of pavement defect progression across seasonal surveys. A single condition survey cannot distinguish stable imperfections from rapidly worsening defects. In the reported study, georeferenced footway images collected every three months were registered and processed to track cracking, uplift and missing paving units at object level. Tree-root-related uplift progressed faster than other defect classes and accounted for most newly hazardous segments. A subset was inspected in the field after each acquisition round.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Pressure-sensing stroller assessment of rolling resistance on pedestrian routes. A stroller instrumented with wheel force sensors and an inertial unit was pushed along routes with different gradients and paving types at a controlled pace. Repeated trials separated surface effects from slope and operator variation. Rolling resistance affects caregivers, wheelchair users and people transporting goods but is rarely included in walkability assessment. Uneven unit paving produced sustained resistance increases even where visual audits rated the surface as acceptable.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Manual audit of school walking routes using a checklist. Auditors recorded sidewalk presence, crossing facilities, traffic and maintenance on paper forms, with duplicate visits used to assess reliability. Scores were mapped and discussed with school staff. Trained observers inspected routes to identify barriers faced by children. Inter-rater reliability was highest for sidewalk presence and lowest for maintenance and perceived security items.
label: Not related

text: Computer vision inventory of tactile paving colour contrast and continuity. Tactile guidance is less useful when visual contrast is weak or paths terminate unexpectedly. Methodologically, street-level images were processed to detect tactile surfaces, estimate colour contrast against surrounding pavement and trace continuity through intersections. Measurements were validated against spectrophotometer readings and on-site route checks. Low contrast was particularly common after resurfacing projects in which tactile units had been retained but adjacent materials changed.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Focus groups on barriers to walking in suburban communities. Residents discussed environmental and social factors that discouraged local walking. Methodologically, facilitated sessions were transcribed and thematically coded, with participants drawing problematic locations on printed maps. Themes included traffic, poor maintenance and lack of destinations. Participants emphasised traffic speed, discontinuous sidewalks and the absence of everyday destinations.
label: Not related

text: Radar measurement of vehicle approach speed at unsignalised pedestrian crossings. Crossing comfort depends on the speed and yielding behaviour of approaching traffic, not only on geometric provision. Compact roadside radar units recorded trajectories at 28 unsignalised crossings while cameras classified pedestrian arrival, waiting and acceptance events. Synchronised observations allowed speed profiles to be linked to individual crossing decisions. Higher approach-speed variability, rather than mean speed alone, was associated with longer pedestrian waiting times.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Photograph-based stated preference experiment for crossing comfort. Respondents evaluated hypothetical crossing situations shown in edited street photographs. Traffic volume, refuge provision and sidewalk width were systematically manipulated, and choice models estimated attribute preferences. Participant characteristics were collected by questionnaire. Refuge islands and shorter crossing distances increased stated comfort, especially among older respondents.
label: Not related

text: Walking interviews about neighbourhood attachment and route choice. Participants joined researchers on self-selected walks and provided recorded commentary about landmarks, identity and change. The research examined how social memory influenced residents' preferred walking routes. Narratives were coded and mapped. Route preferences were shaped by familiar landmarks and social ties as much as by directness.
label: Not related

text: Urban heatwave scenarios generated with a regional climate model. Researchers downscaled future climate projections to estimate neighbourhood air temperature under alternative emissions pathways and urban growth assumptions. Land-cover fractions and building density were used as model inputs, and results were summarised by district. The analysis identified areas likely to experience larger future warming, but it did not collect pedestrian-height measurements or evaluate specific walking routes.
label: Not related

text: Video analytics of turning conflicts across raised pedestrian tables. Fixed cameras tracked pedestrians, cyclists and turning vehicles at six treatments, deriving time-to-collision, yielding and path deviation measures. Trajectory accuracy was checked against manually annotated clips. Raised tables are intended to prioritise walking, yet driver interactions differ according to layout and traffic conditions. Sites with tighter corner radii produced more yielding and fewer pedestrian evasive movements than visually similar sites with flared approaches.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Mobile eye tracking of visual search before complex road crossings. Pedestrians may fail to detect relevant traffic streams when crossings require attention to several directions. Methodologically, participants wore eye-tracking glasses while approaching multilane junctions, and gaze events were mapped to vehicles, signal heads, kerbs and refuge areas identified in scene video. Crossing decisions were coded independently from the gaze record. Longer visual search and repeated checks were observed where turning movements were poorly channelised.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Microsimulation of crowding after station redesign. Alternative concourse layouts were evaluated before construction. Methodologically, a pedestrian simulation was calibrated with generic speed-density relationships and forecast passenger demand. Queue lengths and transfer times were compared across designs. The preferred layout reduced predicted transfer times and queue spillback under the highest demand scenario.
label: Not related

text: Body-worn microclimate sensing beneath contrasting street tree canopies. Tree species and canopy structure can produce different pedestrian thermal conditions despite similar overhead cover. Walkers carried instruments measuring air temperature, humidity, globe temperature and shortwave radiation along matched shaded segments dominated by four tree species. Transects were repeated under comparable weather and corrected using a nearby reference station. Dense low canopies reduced radiant load most strongly, while sparse high canopies preserved ventilation but provided less midday protection.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Hydrodynamic simulation of flood depth on pedestrian links. Terrain and drainage data drove a rainfall-runoff model, and predicted depth was intersected with a pedestrian network. Surface-water scenarios were used to identify walking routes likely to become impassable. Historical incident reports provided qualitative comparison. Low-lying links near drainage outfalls were predicted to become impassable earliest across the tested storms.
label: Not related

text: Wearable ultraviolet dosimetry for evaluating shade continuity on school walks. Short gaps in shade can dominate cumulative ultraviolet exposure on routine journeys. To address this, children's route volunteers wore shoulder-mounted dosimeters and GNSS units while walking recommended school paths under clear-sky conditions. Street imagery and hemispherical photographs quantified canopy and built shade at each segment. Routes with similar average canopy differed markedly in exposure because one contained long unprotected crossing approaches.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Synthetic noise propagation along a proposed pedestrian boulevard. Acoustic performance of a future design was estimated before implementation. To address this, a standard propagation model used forecast traffic, facade geometry and surface absorption to predict sound levels. Scenario maps compared barrier and planting options. Barrier and planting scenarios reduced predicted levels near the boulevard edge, with smaller changes at upper facades.
label: Not related

text: Pedestrian-height sensor network for monitoring nocturnal heat release. Night-time heat can reduce the usability of walking routes during prolonged hot periods. In the reported study, compact temperature, humidity and globe-temperature stations were installed at pedestrian height along streets with different materials and enclosure for an entire summer. Stone-paved enclosed streets cooled slowly and maintained elevated comfort indices several hours after sunset. Sensors were inter-calibrated and compared with a rooftop weather station.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Mobile measurement of wind gusts along elevated pedestrian connections. An instrumented trolley carrying a fast-response anemometer traversed elevated connections during multiple wind directions, while position and parapet geometry were logged. Repeated runs quantified uncertainty caused by walking speed. Bridges and elevated walkways can expose pedestrians to wind conditions not represented by nearby ground stations. Gust amplification was greatest near changes in enclosure and corresponded with locations where users frequently paused or turned back.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Depth-camera stair detection for a powered wheelchair. A forward-facing depth camera classified ramps, steps and drop-offs and triggered speed reduction on a powered wheelchair. Prototype testing occurred on indoor and outdoor courses. The work developed an assistive controller to avoid hazardous level changes. The prototype detected downward steps reliably and reduced approach speed before most hazards.
label: Not related

text: Coupled sensing of shade, humidity and walking pace in a tropical market district. Thermal exposure and pedestrian behaviour vary rapidly around awnings, stalls and open intersections. Methodologically, researchers combined mobile microclimate sensors with overhead video that estimated walking speed and stopping duration along market streets. Measurements covered weekdays and market days under similar synoptic conditions. Continuous awnings lowered radiant exposure and were associated with slower, more sustained pedestrian activity rather than rapid passage.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Visual-inertial localisation of warehouse robots around marked pedestrian lanes. Autonomous carts fused camera features, wheel odometry and inertial measurements to maintain position in a logistics facility where workers and vehicles shared circulation space. Tests focused on localisation error, route completion and recovery after temporary occlusion. Painted pedestrian lanes appeared in the sensor data as map landmarks, but the work neither assessed their accessibility nor measured a public walking environment.
label: Not related

text: Distributed particulate sensing at pedestrian breathing height near bus corridors. Pollutant concentrations measured on rooftops may underestimate exposure beside idling buses. Low-cost particulate sensors were mounted at breathing height along footways near stops, crossings and mid-block segments, with calibration against a reference instrument. Data were matched to bus arrival records and wind observations. Short concentration peaks occurred around stop clusters and were substantially reduced where boarding islands increased separation from traffic.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Reinforcement learning for socially compliant robot motion. A mobile service robot learned to navigate among pedestrians while respecting social distance. Policies were trained in simulation and tested using onboard range sensing in a pedestrian plaza. Evaluation focused on collision avoidance, travel time and personal-space intrusion. The learned policy reduced personal-space intrusion while preserving acceptable travel time.
label: Not related

text: Computer vision guidance following tactile paving. Vanishing-point and line-detection algorithms generated steering commands under varied illumination. An autonomous mobility aid used camera images to remain aligned with tactile guidance surfaces. Experiments assessed tracking accuracy and recovery from occlusion. Tracking remained stable through moderate occlusion but deteriorated when surface contrast was low.
label: Not related

text: Simultaneous air-quality and noise sensing on alternative routes to transit. Route recommendations based solely on distance can direct walkers through environmentally burdensome streets. To address this, volunteers carried particulate, nitrogen dioxide and sound sensors on paired routes between residential blocks and rail stations. Repeated morning and evening journeys controlled for temporal variation. Interior routes were quieter and cleaner but included steeper segments, demonstrating the need for multidimensional pedestrian route assessment.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Procedurally generated navigation data for sensory-substitution devices. A synthetic environment was created to train compact policies for blind travellers. To address this, rendered semantic maps and collision rewards supported reinforcement learning, followed by transfer tests in indoor scenes. The contribution concerned model efficiency and assistive feedback. Compact policies transferred to unseen indoor layouts and operated within the latency limits of the prototype device.
label: Not related

text: Chemical sensing of de-icing residues on winter pedestrian surfaces. Portable conductivity and moisture sensors sampled treated footways after snowfall events, accompanied by friction tests and georeferenced imagery. Routes maintained under different service contracts were compared. De-icing treatments improve traction but may leave residues that affect surface condition and nearby vegetation. Excessive residual concentrations were common where drainage was poor, indicating that maintenance quality involves both safety and environmental performance.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Semantic segmentation of visual complexity along routes used by older pedestrians. Cluttered visual scenes can complicate orientation even when physical accessibility is adequate. Methodologically, panoramic imagery was segmented into signs, vehicles, vegetation, facades and street furniture, and entropy-based complexity measures were computed at eye level. Older participants completed accompanied walks and marked locations they found confusing. Reported disorientation clustered where sign density and foreground obstruction were both high.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Camera-based monitoring of bicycle parking occupancy at transit stations. Fixed cameras detected bicycles, empty racks and improperly parked cycles at station entrances throughout the day. Occupancy profiles were validated against manual inventories and used to identify locations requiring additional capacity. The system analysed bicycle-storage demand and obstruction of rack areas; it did not derive pedestrian route quality, sidewalk continuity or broader walkability indicators.
label: Not related

text: Night-time street imagery for detecting glare and dark adaptation zones. Abrupt transitions between bright commercial frontages and poorly lit side streets can impair pedestrian vision. Calibrated night imagery was analysed to estimate luminance distributions, glare sources and adaptation demand along continuous walking routes. Portable illuminance readings and observer assessments validated the extracted measures. The largest adaptation demands occurred at arcade exits and illuminated advertising panels facing narrow footways.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: App-derived micromobility demand and scooter rebalancing. Shared-scooter trip records and vehicle GPS pings were analysed to forecast hourly demand and optimise redistribution between service zones. Models incorporated weather, calendar effects and proximity to transit. The revised strategy reduced empty-station events and operator travel distance. Although trip origins frequently occurred near sidewalks, the study did not sense physical pedestrian-environment dimensions.
label: Not related

text: Image-derived human-scale enclosure compared with pedestrian comfort ratings. Depth-estimated street panoramas were used to derive directional enclosure and visual escape measures across residential blocks. Building-height-to-width ratios calculated from plan data do not fully reflect vegetation, setbacks and openings visible to walkers. Participants rated comfort during in-situ walks rather than from photographs. Asymmetric enclosure and long blank boundaries predicted lower comfort more consistently than conventional canyon ratios.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Inertial vibration mapping of bicycle lane pavement. Handlebar-mounted accelerometers and GPS generated a roughness indicator for protected and painted lanes. Cyclists recorded surface vibration to support maintenance of a bicycle network. The index was compared with cyclist comfort surveys. Roughness values were highest on painted lanes affected by utility cuts and drainage covers.
label: Not related

text: Detecting sheltered route continuity from street and aerial oblique imagery. Protection from rain depends on whether canopies connect along the actual pedestrian path. To address this, a fusion model combined street-level and oblique images to map arcades, awnings, transit shelters and gaps in cover. Field checks recorded whether mapped elements protected the usable footway rather than only the facade. Commercial centres had high total canopy area but poor route continuity because protection repeatedly stopped at side-street crossings.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Repeated imagery assessment of greenery maintenance at pedestrian eye level. Vegetation can support walking only when pruning, health and clearance are maintained. In the reported study, street images collected over three years were processed to estimate foliage density, dead canopy, low branches and obstruction of lighting or signs. Declining greenery quality was detectable before canopy-loss statistics from overhead imagery showed meaningful change. Arborist inspections validated condition classes on selected corridors.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Computer vision analysis of driver search behaviour for parking. Instrumented vehicles were used to understand how drivers behaved while seeking street parking. In the reported study, eye tracking, vehicle telemetry and physiological sensors recorded speed, gaze and workload on urban routes. Parking search increased off-road glances and subjective workload while reducing mean vehicle speed. Outcomes focused on driving safety and attention.
label: Not related

text: Street-view measurement of seating orientation and shade at resting places. Object detection located public seating, while image geometry and solar modelling estimated whether seats faced pedestrian activity and received shade during afternoon hours. A field survey checked occupancy and physical condition. The usefulness of benches depends on their position, orientation and microclimatic setting, not simply their presence. Benches with partial shade and views toward active frontages were used more frequently than exposed seating placed behind the walking line.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Traffic-camera classification of bicycle-pedestrian conflicts. Tracks were classified by mode and conflict indicators were calculated for crossing events. The primary objective was cycling safety and operational conflict management. Video data were analysed to detect interactions on shared-use paths. Conflict rates were highest where bicycle paths crossed pedestrian desire lines at shallow angles.
label: Not related

text: Bluetooth-assisted calibration of pedestrian counts on festival streets. Temporary events alter pedestrian volumes and device-carrying patterns, complicating passive wireless counting. Methodologically, bluetooth detections were collected alongside thermal-camera counts at gateways during ordinary days and a week-long festival. Time-varying calibration factors were estimated by hour and crowd composition. A fixed conversion factor substantially underestimated family-oriented periods, whereas adaptive calibration reproduced observed event peaks.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Privacy-preserving edge cameras for directional footfall monitoring. Continuous pedestrian counts can inform maintenance and public-space management while avoiding storage of identifiable imagery. Edge devices converted video frames directly into anonymous tracks and directional counts at neighbourhood centres, discarding images after processing. Counts were compared with manual observations under different lighting and crowding conditions. Accuracy remained stable except during heavy umbrella use, and the system revealed distinct through-movement and local stopping patterns.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Automated facade damage detection for post-storm insurance inspection. Vehicle-mounted cameras captured building exteriors after a severe wind event, and a detection network identified broken glazing, detached cladding and roof-edge damage. Claims inspectors verified a sample of alerts, and the system accelerated triage of affected properties. Images were collected from streets, but the measured objects concerned building damage rather than pedestrian conditions.
label: Not related

text: Wi-Fi sensing of dwell and through-movement in pedestrian plazas. An array of synchronised Wi-Fi receivers estimated anonymous device trajectories across plaza zones, with camera observations used only for aggregate calibration. A single occupancy total does not distinguish people passing through from those using a public space. Trajectory duration and spatial persistence separated dwell from passage. Seating additions increased dwell without materially changing through-flow, a change that conventional gate counts would have missed.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Computer vision inventory of tobacco branding around schools. Researchers processed geotagged street photographs to detect shop signs, branded displays and promotional colours within walking distance of secondary schools. Automated counts were compared with manual coding and linked to neighbourhood deprivation. Branding exposure was higher near major commercial roads. The imagery served a public-health marketing study rather than measurement of walkability dimensions.
label: Not related

text: Computer vision measurement of pedestrian platooning at narrow bottlenecks. Narrow sections can cause pedestrians to reorganise into single-file groups long before density reaches crowding thresholds. To address this, overhead cameras tracked individual paths through temporary and permanent constrictions, deriving lateral spacing, overtaking and platoon length. The automated measures were verified on manually annotated intervals. Single-file organisation emerged at wider effective widths than assumed in standard level-of-service guidance when opposing flows were balanced.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Vehicle imagery for municipal litter-cleansing schedules. Service vehicles collected images to identify litter, overflowing bins and illegal dumping. To address this, a detection model produced route-level waste maps that were used to reorganise cleansing rounds. Performance was compared with complaint records. The resulting waste maps supported revised cleansing schedules and reduced repeat complaints in pilot districts.
label: Not related

text: Thermal counters for seasonal use of riverside walking paths. Understanding when paths are used supports interpretation of environmental measurements and investment outcomes. In the reported study, battery-powered thermal counters recorded direction and volume at multiple entrances for eighteen months, with periodic manual calibration and weather linkage. Use responded more strongly to wind exposure than temperature, and sheltered segments retained activity during otherwise unfavourable days. Counts were cleaned for group occlusion and maintenance interruptions.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Image-based urban tree disease surveillance. A classifier detected crown dieback, discolouration and trunk lesions and prioritised arborist inspections. Field diagnosis verified selected alerts. A citywide programme used street images to identify symptoms of tree disease. The classifier identified early crown decline and reduced the number of trees requiring immediate field inspection.
label: Not related

text: Passive infrared monitoring of footway occupancy beside school entrances. Short, intense occupancy peaks can create accessibility problems even where daily pedestrian totals are modest. Methodologically, passive infrared arrays and time-of-flight sensors monitored usable footway zones during arrival and dismissal periods at twelve schools. Synchronous video samples calibrated occupancy estimates and distinguished adults from clustered groups only at aggregate level. Critical crowding was driven by waiting caregivers and occurred mainly where parked vehicles constrained the available edge space.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Acoustic sensors for urban bird diversity in parks. Autonomous recorders monitored bird communities across parks during the breeding season. Methodologically, species calls were classified and related to habitat structure and surrounding development. The outcome was biodiversity. Species richness was highest in larger parks with complex vegetation structure and lower surrounding built density.
label: Not related

text: Continuous observation of pedestrian route choice around flooded underpasses. Minor flooding can alter walking networks before routes become completely impassable. Water-level sensors and camera-based counts monitored an underpass and nearby alternatives during rainfall events. Route shifts were related to measured depth, duration and lighting conditions. Pedestrians began avoiding the underpass at shallow depths, with older users diverting earlier than the overall population.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Street-camera detection of commercial vacancy for tax administration. The study automated updates to a municipal business-property register. Storefront imagery was processed to identify closure signs, boarded windows and changes in business names. Outputs were checked against licensing data. Automated alerts improved the timeliness of registry updates, particularly in rapidly changing commercial streets.
label: Not related

text: Thermal imaging of building-envelope heat loss. Vehicle-mounted thermal cameras recorded building surfaces and detected anomalous heat signatures, with audits confirming insulation defects. Researchers assessed facade energy performance during winter nights. Results supported retrofit targeting. Heat-loss anomalies were concentrated around window frames and uninsulated roof junctions in older buildings.
label: Not related

text: Detecting public toilet accessibility from entrance imagery and depth data. Public toilets extend the usable walking range of older adults and people with medical needs. In the reported study, a mobile mapping survey captured entrances to public facilities, and a model extracted steps, door width, signage and turning space from images and depth measurements. Facilities were geographically widespread, but accessible entrances were concentrated in recently refurbished districts. Accessibility specialists reviewed uncertain cases.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Satellite mapping of impervious cover for urban flood vulnerability. Multispectral imagery from several years was classified into built surfaces, vegetation and water, then combined with terrain and drainage data to model neighbourhood flood susceptibility. Accuracy was evaluated against municipal land-cover records and historical flood reports. The overhead analysis supported citywide resilience planning but did not measure conditions experienced along pedestrian routes.
label: Not related

text: Sensor-assisted audit of handrail temperature and usability in extreme weather. Surface temperature sensors and mobile imagery assessed handrail continuity, height, clearance and thermal condition along stepped pedestrian connections. Measurements were repeated across summer and winter extremes. Handrails support walking on steep routes but can become uncomfortable to touch under intense sun or cold. Dark metal rails frequently exceeded comfortable contact temperatures, while shaded timber rails maintained more usable conditions.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Drone photogrammetry of coastal dunes near an urban beach. Orthomosaics and surface models were generated and compared across seasons. The work supported coastal conservation. Unmanned aerial surveys mapped dune morphology and erosion. Repeated models documented dune retreat and local recovery after restoration works.
label: Not related

text: Multimodal assessment of pedestrian route quality around hospitals. Hospital approaches must accommodate users with limited mobility, sensory impairment and heightened sensitivity to environmental stress. Methodologically, a survey rig combined panoramic imagery, lidar, noise, air-quality and illuminance sensing along routes from transit stops to hospital entrances. Attributes were aggregated into separate physical-access and environmental-comfort profiles rather than a single score. The shortest approaches were often the least comfortable, and route deficiencies varied sharply between opposite sides of the same street.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Aerial imagery classification of road and sidewalk pixels for driving maps. A remote-sensing model segmented transport surfaces across a metropolitan area. Methodologically, high-resolution overhead imagery was classified into roads, sidewalks and vegetation to enrich autonomous-driving maps. Evaluation focused on pixel accuracy. The model improved map completeness for autonomous-driving applications, particularly at complex junctions.
label: Not related

text: Wearable gait signatures for continuous user authentication. Participants wore ankle-mounted inertial sensors during ordinary indoor walking, and temporal gait features were used to distinguish authorised device users from impostors. Authentication performance was evaluated across footwear and walking-speed changes. The study treated gait as a biometric signal and did not examine the environmental quality or accessibility of the surfaces traversed.
label: Not related

text: Detecting snow-clearance continuity with repeated pedestrian-level imaging. A route is only as usable as its least-cleared segment after snowfall. To address this, cameras mounted on maintenance inspection bicycles captured footways at regular intervals, and segmentation distinguished clear pavement, compacted snow and ploughed ridges at crossings. Field teams verified selected classifications and recorded clearance times. Priority routes often contained isolated uncleared links at property boundaries, substantially delaying network recovery.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Activity-monitor validation for people using canes. Researchers assessed whether step counters remained accurate when mounted on the leg or walking aid. In the reported study, participants completed indoor and outdoor trials over several surfaces while video supplied reference counts. Leg-mounted placement produced more accurate step counts than mounting the device on the cane. Device sensitivity was compared by placement.
label: Not related

text: Repeated point-cloud assessment of curbside dining encroachment. Compact mobile lidar scans were collected during morning setup, lunch and evening periods, and tables, barriers and queues were mapped relative to the legal footway clearance zone. Manual observations verified business activity and temporary object classes. Outdoor dining layouts change daily and can compromise a continuous accessible path. Even compliant furniture layouts became restrictive when customer queues formed outside designated areas.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Systematic review of emerging technologies for walkability assessment. The review compared GIS indices, audits, street imagery, lidar and wearable sensing reported in prior research. Databases were searched and methods were categorised by spatial scale and construct coverage. Research gaps and reporting recommendations were proposed. Because the article collected no primary environmental data, it is not itself a sensing study.
label: Not related

text: Protocol for a national urban exposure data platform. The protocol specified data sources, linkage units and future model development. A consortium described plans to harmonise air quality, greenness, climate, transport and walkability data. Most initial indicators came from existing national datasets. The paper presents infrastructure and methodology rather than an implemented sensor-based measurement of pedestrian environments.
label: Not related

text: Social-media sentiment toward a proposed pedestrianisation scheme. Public posts and online comments were collected before and after consultation on closing a central street to through traffic. Natural-language models classified support, concerns and recurring topics, while user locations were aggregated at district level. Sentiment became more favourable after design revisions. The evidence consisted of text-based opinion data rather than sensor measurements of the street environment.
label: Not related

text: Bluetooth and infrared counting to characterise pedestrian volumes on a waterfront promenade. Understanding temporal patterns of pedestrian use supports management of public space. Infrared beam counters and Bluetooth detectors were deployed at eight gateways along a waterfront promenade for one year. Counts were corrected for device-specific detection rates estimated through manual calibration sessions. Seasonal, weekly and diurnal profiles were derived and related to weather records, revealing strong sensitivity of promenade use to thermal conditions and precipitation.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Depth camera assessment of step height and kerb geometry at pedestrian crossings. Kerb geometry determines whether a crossing is negotiable by users with reduced mobility. A handheld depth camera was used to capture the crossing geometry at 340 intersections, from which kerb height, ramp gradient and gutter depth were reconstructed. Measurements were compared with manual gauge readings on a validation subset, showing millimetre-level agreement. Nearly half of surveyed crossings exceeded the maximum permissible kerb height, and non-compliance was more frequent on secondary streets.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Wearable heart rate variability sensing during walking in contrasting urban settings. Physiological response provides an objective complement to self-reported evaluation of walking environments. Participants completed matched-length walking routes through a busy arterial corridor and a residential street while wearing chest-mounted electrocardiography sensors. Heart rate variability indices were computed per segment and matched to streetscape attributes derived from image segmentation. Reduced parasympathetic indices were consistently observed on segments with high traffic exposure and low vegetation.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Detecting street furniture and resting opportunities from mobile mapping data. Availability of benches and resting places is a determinant of walkability for older pedestrians but is seldom inventoried. Mobile mapping point clouds and co-registered imagery were processed to detect benches, bollards, waste bins and shelters along the pedestrian network. Detections were classified by type and georeferenced. Spatial analysis revealed that mean distance between consecutive resting opportunities exceeded 400 metres across most of the residential network, well above recommended thresholds for older users.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Automated detection of pavement surface defects on urban footways using image analysis. Surface defects create trip hazards and reduce comfort. Images captured by a pedestrian-borne camera rig along 55 km of footways were analysed with a segmentation model trained to detect cracking, uplift, missing units and ponding. Detection performance was validated against a manual condition survey. Defect density was strongly associated with tree root proximity and with footway age, and results supported prioritisation of maintenance works.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Estimating pedestrian-level wind conditions with distributed anemometry in a high-rise district. Wind discomfort can render otherwise attractive pedestrian spaces unusable. Compact ultrasonic anemometers were installed at pedestrian height at 24 locations across a high-rise district and recorded continuously for twelve months. Measured gust equivalent mean speeds were classified against established comfort criteria. Several plaza locations exceeded discomfort thresholds for more than 20 percent of daylight hours, and measurements were used to validate previously published simulation results for the same district.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Segmenting street-level imagery to assess weather protection along pedestrian routes. Continuous shelter influences walking in both hot and rainy climates. This study segmented street-level images to detect arcades, canopies, awnings and covered walkways along pedestrian routes in a subtropical city, computing the proportion of each route length under cover. Automated estimates were validated against field observation on sampled routes. Coverage was highly uneven, with continuous protection largely confined to commercial cores while residential connectors remained fully exposed.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Transit accessibility and station area development in a polycentric region. Coordinating land use with transit provision is central to sustainable regional planning. This study computes station area accessibility using network analysis of scheduled service data and parcel-level land use records. Development intensity around stations is compared across corridors and time periods. Results indicate that intensification has concentrated around a limited subset of stations, and policy implications for coordinating growth with service provision are discussed.
label: Not related

text: Deep learning classification of building facade materials for energy retrofit prioritisation. Retrofit programmes require knowledge of the existing building stock that is often unavailable. Street-level images were processed with a classification model to identify facade materials, glazing ratios and apparent construction period for residential buildings. Predictions were validated against a sample of surveyed properties. The resulting stock characterisation was used to estimate retrofit potential and to prioritise intervention districts.
label: Not related

text: Wearable sensing of running biomechanics on outdoor surfaces. Reducing tendon loading during running may lower injury risk. Recreational runners completed outdoor trials on a concrete surface at controlled speeds while instrumented with inertial sensors and pressure insoles. Ground contact time was manipulated across conditions and resulting changes in estimated tendon force and cadence were analysed. Increasing ground contact time reduced peak estimated force but induced compensatory cadence changes.
label: Not related

text: Point cloud processing for heritage facade documentation. Conservation of historic buildings requires accurate geometric records. Terrestrial laser scanning was used to capture facades along a protected street, and processing routines were developed to segment architectural elements and to detect deformation relative to reference geometry. Accuracy was assessed against total station measurements. The workflow supports condition monitoring and the preparation of conservation documentation.
label: Not related

text: Mobile phone signalling data for estimating intercity travel demand. Understanding aggregate mobility patterns supports transport planning. Anonymised mobile network signalling records were processed to infer origin-destination flows between urban areas, with algorithms to distinguish residents from visitors and to assign trip purposes. Estimates were validated against household travel survey benchmarks. The approach provides continuous demand estimates at a fraction of the cost of conventional surveys.
label: Not related

text: Georeferenced audio recording for characterising acoustic diversity of pedestrian streets in a Mediterranean city. Acoustic environment contributes to whether a street is pleasant to walk. Binaural recorders carried along fixed routes captured continuous audio, from which psychoacoustic descriptors including loudness, sharpness and roughness were computed alongside conventional level metrics. Recordings were segmented and clustered. Streets dominated by human voices and water features clustered separately from traffic-dominated streets, and cluster membership predicted independently collected pleasantness ratings.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Low-cost distributed sensing of footway occupancy in a market district. Understanding when footways become crowded supports management of shared space. Passive infrared and time-of-flight units were mounted at pedestrian height along footways in a market district and recorded occupancy at short intervals for six months. Counts were calibrated against synchronised video. Occupancy exceeded comfortable density thresholds during market hours on segments where stalls reduced usable width, quantifying a conflict previously reported only anecdotally.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Detecting encroachment of informal commerce onto footways from street imagery. Informal trading occupies footway space in many cities, with consequences for pedestrian flow. Street imagery collected at multiple times of day was processed with a detection model trained to identify stalls, displayed goods and temporary structures within the footway envelope. Occupied width was estimated per segment and compared across time slices. Occupancy peaked in the late afternoon and reduced usable width below one metre on a third of commercial segments.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Instrumented walking to characterise perceived and measured slope burden in a hillside settlement. Steep informal settlements pose particular walking challenges. Residents carried devices combining barometric altimetry, inertial sensing and satellite positioning during habitual trips while providing periodic effort ratings through a mobile prompt. Measured gradient and cumulative ascent were related to reported effort. Ratings rose sharply above a gradient threshold, and the identified threshold was used to prioritise locations for stairs and handrail installation.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Machine learning prediction of traffic congestion from loop detector data. Congestion forecasting supports network management. Loop detector records across an arterial network were used to train recurrent models predicting occupancy and speed at multiple horizons. Model performance was compared with historical average and autoregressive baselines. Gains were largest during incident conditions, and the models were integrated into an operational dashboard for the traffic management centre.
label: Not related

text: Assessing green roof cooling potential with rooftop instrumentation. Green roofs are promoted as an urban heat mitigation measure. Paired instrumented plots on conventional and vegetated roofs recorded surface and air temperature, substrate moisture and energy flux over two summers. Differences in surface temperature and sensible heat flux were quantified across weather conditions. Cooling benefit was greatest under high radiation and adequate moisture, with implications for irrigation scheduling.
label: Not related

text: Detection of illegal parking from fixed cameras for enforcement support. Unauthorised parking affects traffic operation and enforcement resources. Fixed cameras coupled with detection and plate recognition were deployed at enforcement hotspots and produced continuous records of violations by time and duration. Detections were validated against officer records. The system supported redeployment of enforcement patrols and reduced average violation duration in treated locations.
label: Not related

text: Longitudinal analysis of urban expansion using historical aerial photography. Understanding growth patterns supports planning policy evaluation. Historical aerial photographs spanning six decades were orthorectified and classified to delineate built-up extent at ten-year intervals. Growth metrics including compactness and fragmentation were computed. The analysis identifies distinct expansion phases and relates them to successive regional planning frameworks.
label: Not related

text: Wearable sensing of occupational physical workload in construction. Excessive workload contributes to musculoskeletal disorders. Workers wore inertial sensors and heart rate monitors during shifts, and posture, movement intensity and cardiovascular strain were derived. Task categories were annotated by observers. Several task categories exceeded recommended strain thresholds, supporting task rotation recommendations.
label: Not related

text: Comparison of open and proprietary road network datasets for routing applications. Routing quality depends on underlying network data. This study compares completeness, positional accuracy and attribute richness of open and proprietary road network datasets across several regions, using reference survey data. Differences in coverage were concentrated in recently developed areas and in service roads. Implications for routing applications and for reproducibility of accessibility research are discussed.
label: Not related

text: Evaluating a smartphone application for encouraging walking through gamification. Behaviour change applications are widely deployed but unevenly evaluated. This randomised trial allocated participants to a gamified walking application or a control application without game elements, with step counts recorded by the application over twelve weeks. Retention and step count trajectories were compared. Modest short-term gains attenuated after week six, and engagement declined steeply across both arms.
label: Not related

text: Spatial analysis of green space provision inequity using administrative data. Equitable access to green space is a policy concern. Park polygons from municipal records were combined with population data at fine spatial resolution to compute provision and proximity measures for socioeconomic groups. Inequity indices were computed and compared across cities. Provision gaps were largest for high-density lower-income neighbourhoods, and the analysis relies entirely on administrative datasets.
label: Not related

text: Mobile laser profiling of crossfall transitions along accessible walking routes. Abrupt changes in crossfall can destabilise wheelchair users even when average sidewalk slope appears compliant. A push-cart laser scanner surveyed priority routes around hospitals, and local planes were fitted at half-metre intervals to derive crossfall transitions, clear width and ramp geometry. Comparison with digital inclinometer measurements showed close agreement and identified clusters of rapid crossfall change near driveways. The segment-level inventory supports targeted accessibility repairs rather than whole-street reconstruction.
label: Sensing of walkability dimension

text: Comparing composite walkability scores for predicting commuting mode. Different index formulations may classify the same neighbourhood inconsistently. In the empirical work, four GIS-based scores were calculated from census, parcel and road-network data and related to commute mode reported in a household travel survey.
